subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: A fugue opens with which compositional procedure?
options: A subject stated alone then imitated by successive voices
questions.explain: A fugue begins with a subject announced in one voice, answered imitatively by entering voices.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is...?
options: Singing in strict unison with the bass line
Singing only the written lyrics with no variation
Vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables to imitate an instrument
questions.explain: Scat singing improvises wordless, nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an improvising instrument.

questions.q: In film music, 'underscoring' (or underscore) most accurately means...?
options: The lyrics printed beneath a song
A loud climactic fanfare during the titles
Background music supporting a scene's mood or action, typically not heard by the characters
Music that the on-screen characters can hear (diegetic music)
questions.explain: Underscoring is non-diegetic background music that supports a scene's emotional or dramatic content.

questions.q: The whole-tone scale, favoured by Debussy, divides the octave into how many equal steps?
questions.explain: The whole-tone scale consists of six pitches a whole tone apart, lacking semitones and a clear tonic.

questions.q: Brahms is generally regarded as a Romantic composer who upheld which trait?
options: Classical formal structures within a Romantic idiom
questions.explain: Brahms combined Romantic expression with Classical forms such as the symphony and sonata, in the absolute-music tradition.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
The music has no fixed pulse
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.

questions.q: The Argentine 'tango' is most associated with which instrument providing its characteristic sound?
questions.explain: The bandoneón, a button accordion, gives the tango its distinctive timbre.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.

questions.q: The relative minor of G major is which key?
questions.explain: The relative minor shares the key signature of G major (one sharp) and is E minor.

questions.q: In fusion music, an artist such as Ravi Shankar collaborating with Western musicians most exemplifies...?
options: The blending of Indian classical techniques (raga, tala, sitar) with Western elements
questions.explain: Such collaborations blend Indian classical features like raga, tala and sitar with Western musical elements.

questions.q: In the context of performance, 'idiomatic writing' for an instrument means...?
options: Writing that ignores the instrument's natural strengths
Writing only in the treble clef
Writing that suits the technique, range and characteristic capabilities of the instrument
questions.explain: Idiomatic writing exploits the natural technique, range and strengths of the specific instrument.

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
A major seventh chord on the tonic
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: A German augmented sixth chord contains which intervals above the bass?
options: Major third, augmented fourth and augmented sixth
Major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth
Major third and augmented sixth only
questions.explain: The German sixth comprises a major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth above the bass note.

questions.q: In C major, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is which quality?
questions.explain: The triad on the leading note in a major key is diminished, comprising B-D-F in C major.

questions.q: A 'walking bass' line in jazz is most characterised by which feature?
options: A sustained pedal note held under the harmony
A steady stream of crotchets outlining the chords, usually one note per beat
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in even crotchets, typically one note per beat, threading through the chord tones to drive the harmony forward.

questions.q: Chopin's output is dominated by works for which instrument?
questions.explain: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, including nocturnes, mazurkas and ballades.

questions.q: In performance, 'interpretation' refers to...?
options: The performer's expressive choices of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation within the score
Transposing the music to a new key
Playing the notes exactly as printed with no expressive choices
questions.explain: Interpretation is the performer's expressive shaping of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation.

questions.q: Wagner's term for a recurring musical theme associated with a character or idea is which?
questions.explain: Wagner used leitmotifs, short recurring themes representing characters, objects or ideas in his music dramas.

questions.q: The effect known as 'delay' produces which result?
options: A panning of sound between left and right speakers
A widening of the stereo field by phase inversion
One or more distinct repeats (echoes) of the original signal
questions.explain: Delay creates discrete repeats, or echoes, of the original sound.

questions.q: In a typical pop or rock song, the section designed to be the most memorable and which usually contains the title and main hook is the...?
questions.explain: The chorus is the most memorable section, typically stating the title and main hook.

questions.q: The Indonesian 'gamelan' is primarily an ensemble of...?
questions.explain: A gamelan is built chiefly from tuned metallophones, gongs and drums.

questions.q: A 4-3 suspension resolves by which means?
options: The fourth leaps up to the sixth
The fourth steps down to the third
The third rises to the fourth
questions.explain: In a 4-3 suspension the dissonant fourth resolves downwards by step onto the consonant third.

questions.q: The film-scoring technique 'mickey-mousing' refers to...?
options: Music that closely mirrors and synchronises with on-screen action, beat for beat
Improvised jazz played over the closing credits
Recording the score before filming begins
Using cartoon sound effects in live-action films
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing matches the music precisely to on-screen movement, a hallmark of early animation scoring.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: A Picardy third refers to which feature?
options: A third added above the melody
A minor-key piece ending on a major (raised third) tonic chord
A chord built on the third degree
A major piece ending on the minor third
questions.explain: A tierce de Picardie raises the third of the final tonic chord so a minor-key work ends on a major chord.

questions.q: Serialism, as developed by Schoenberg, organises pitches using which device?
questions.explain: Schoenberg's twelve-tone (serial) method orders all twelve chromatic pitches into a tone row that governs the music.

questions.q: Ragtime, popularised by Scott Joplin, is principally characterised by which rhythmic device?
options: A syncopated, off-beat melody set against a steady march-like bass
Continuous polyrhythmic layering of three rhythms
A swung shuffle feel in the bass
Rubato throughout with no fixed pulse
questions.explain: Ragtime sets a syncopated right-hand melody against a regular, march-style stride bass.

questions.q: Gamelan music frequently uses 'interlocking' (kotekan) parts, meaning...?
options: Two parts combine, each playing alternate notes, to create a single faster composite line
All players double the same melody an octave apart
The ensemble plays in strict Western major scales
questions.explain: Interlocking parts dovetail, each playing alternate notes so that together they form one rapid composite line.

questions.q: The standard twelve-bar blues progression in its basic form follows which sequence of chords (in bars)?
questions.explain: The classic twelve-bar blues uses four bars of I, two of IV returning to I, then V-IV-I across the final four bars.
